10.0.0.en: 1 And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea. 2 And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia? 3 For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.

10.1.0.en: This chapter presents to us a picture of the greatness of Ahasuerus, to whom many provinces submitted and paid tribute, and of Mordecai, the second man, "great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed" [3]. The secret of his greatness was the breadth of his heart in love for his brethren and his speaking of peace for the sake of his children. He became a source of blessing for his generation and for the coming generations through his surpassing love.

10.1.1.en: If the whole people were glorified by their deliverance from the enemy, Mordecai, who sought not what was his own but what belonged to others, was glorified more and more.

10.1.2.en: In the Additions to Esther this chapter continues with a review of Mordecai's dream, in which God assured him that He was working through him and Esther for the salvation of their brethren; we have already spoken about this dream.

10.1.3.en: Our good God, who gave Esther and Mordecai the grace of an open mouth and a heart enlarged with love for their brethren, opens our hearts for the edification of every soul, to the glory of God!

10.1.4.en: * You will find the commentaries on the remaining chapters of the book in the commentary of Fr. Antonious Fikry on the Book of Esther.
